newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Reuters poll sees EMU bond play problems.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Reuters poll sees EMU bond play problems.

text.p: Peripheral European bond markets will underperform German Bunds in the short term amid U.S. interest rate and European monetary union worries but will bounce back by the end the year, according to a Reuters poll released on Wednesday.
Of the peripherals, Portugal and Sweden have the most to gain, while French bond yields will continue their steady march on Bunds, the poll of European bond spread forecasts showed.
Gilts, too, will outpace after the British election on May 1.
"The short term outlook is dependent on two things," said David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International in London.

"One is the outright direction of the U.S. market. If we are going to see further rate hikes, then the chances are there would be a fall in bond prices globally, and the risk factor takes people out of peripheries and into the traditional safe havens like Bunds," he said.
The second factor is concerns over a delay to European economic and monetary uion (EMU) and, more specifically, nervousness ahead of German tax data due in May, Brickman said.
The German government is set to release first quarter federal tax receipts and forecasts for the full year in May.
The data will help markets determine Germany's chances for meeting fiscal targets for EMU. If the estimates are low, talk on delay could revive.
The Reuters poll, compiled from 98 forecasts from banks, research houses and academic institutions around Europe, reflects this uncertainty.

An average of forecasts predicts the gap between 10-year Italian and German bonds will widen to 194 basis points by the end of the second quarter from 166 now, the Spain/Germany spread to 106 from 94 and the Portugal/Germany gap to 94 from 86.
But analysts do not expect that weakness to last as Germany takes decisive action to fill any revenue gaps.

"There will be a situation where the German government knows exactly what the hole is and it then moves immediatly to plug it," said Brickman. "The process of convergence is unlikely to be derailed significantly."
By the second half of the year and into the first quarter of the next year, the peripheral markets will be back on track, according to the Reuters poll.
The Italy/Bund gap was expected to settle back down to 167 basis points by the fourth quarter of 1997 and 154 by end-first quarter in 1998. The Spain/Bund gap would shrink to 99 and then 84.
But the stars will be Portugal and Sweden, which will see their spreads narrow to 60 and 103 basis points, respectively, against Bunds by the end of the first quarter next year.
Graham McDevitt, head of bond strategy for Paribas Capital Markets in London, said Spain won his vote. He forecast the gap would shrink to 50 basis points by the end of the year.
"If Spain is going to be in EMU, it's going to trade down to 50 while Sweden's not going to be as tight as that," he said.

The Reuters poll saw continued convergence of French 10-year bonds against Bunds, with the gap shrinking to minus seven basis points by the end of the second quarter from minus 13 now and to minus one basis point by the end of the first quarter next year.
"Within the core, the tendency will be to remain stable," Brickman said. "Everyone believes those countries are there and are ready for EMU."
Gilts will ride out the May 1 election to outperform Bunds by the end of the second quarter as well, according to the poll.
The gilt/Bund gap will slim to 176 basis points from 185 now, then down to 157 by the end of the year and 151 by the first quarter of next year.

"The focus immediately after the election will be the first mini-budget from the Labour government. I suspect that will be a bit of a damp squib," said Robert Prior, European economist at HSBC James Capel. British interest rates would also feature.
"The market feeling is that Labour will be quite tough and will do what needs to be done on interest rates," he said.
The forecasts for each bond were gathered during 48-hour periods since the beginning of April.

The Bund spread forecasts for French, British and Italian benchmarks have also been incorporated into the Reuters survey of independent long-term forecasts for the G7 economies, which is being updated during April.
